newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CEN.BANK BOUGHT 300 BLN BFR OF FOREX IN 96.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CEN.BANK BOUGHT 300 BLN BFR OF FOREX IN 96.

text.p: The Belgian central bank said it bought about 300 billion Belgian francs worth of foreign exchange in 1996 to limit the rise of the franc.

"We bought enormous amounts of foreign currencies last year to prevent a further appreciation of the franc," governor Alfons Verplaetse told a news conference on the bank's annual report on Wednesday. His comments were embargoed for Friday.
"As you know Belgian industrialists do not want (a franc that is too strong)," he added.
In April 1996 the franc reached a high of 20.53 to the mark, nearly 0.50 percent above its 20.6255 central rate in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).

Verplaetse said he thought that many European central banks, like the Belgian central bank, had "too much currency reserves". According to the latest weekly statement the bank had currency reserves worth 441.25 billion francs.
